subject: MAP: Performance test schedule, test keys, and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Price <oliver.price@brightcart.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP: Performance test schedule, test keys, and acceptance criteria

Hi Oliver,

Thanks again for the productive call today. As discussed, I attached a one-page MAP (MAP-BrightCart-v1.xlsx) that captures the milestones we agreed for the performance evaluation and close timeline. High-level summary below so we have a single source of truth: 

- Objective: Validate production P95 latency <= 350ms for 512-token prompts, TTFT <= 1.2s for cold-starts, sustain 400 requests/sec at 8 concurrent workers for 2x 30m windows.
- Acceptance criteria: Latency and TTFT thresholds above + no data leakage, SDK integration verified in staging.
- Test windows: 2026-11-24 (US West) and 2026-11-29 (US East) — 2 x 30-minute peak runs plus 4 x 15-minute verification runs.
- Deliverables: Redwood provides test accounts, keys (attached), runbook, and operator on-call; BrightCart provides representative prompt sets, expected p95 targets, and a list of test client IPs to whitelist.
- Next steps: BrightCart to confirm window availability and provide final prompt set by EOD Monday 11/23.

I also attached brightcart-test-keys.txt with temporary test credentials (expiry 12/10/2026) and our runbook (redwood-benchmark-runbook.pdf). Sean and Monica are looped for operations and monitoring.

Can you confirm the two proposed windows and share the prompt set and any concurrency constraints we should be aware of?

Best,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: MAP-BrightCart-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), brightcart-test-keys.txt (text), redwood-benchmark-runbook.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: MAP: Performance test schedule, test keys, and acceptance criteria

Hi Tessa —

Thanks for the MAP and the keys. The windows look mostly good; we'd prefer the primary peak run to be 11/24 14:00-14:30 PST (our traffic peak) and a fallback window on 11/30 10:00-10:30 PST if we need a repeat.

A few clarifications:
- Prompt set: we'll send a representative set of 2k prompts (mix of short/long) by Monday EOD.
- Concurrency: our client can simulate up to 12 worker connections; we want to validate both 8 and 12 concurrency to observe degradation curves.
- Keys: please confirm the test keys scope (isolation to staging only, read-only logs).

Also, can your team provide a quick smoke checklist we can run 24 hours before the window? That'll help our SREs allocate capacity.

Oliver
Oliver Price | Head of ML Engineering, BrightCart
oliver.price@brightcart.com

Subject: Re: MAP: Performance test schedule, test keys, and acceptance criteria

Oliver —

Thanks — we can accommodate both 8 and 12 concurrency runs. Confirmed: primary peak 2026-11-24 14:00-14:30 PST, fallback 2026-11-30 10:00-10:30 PST.

About the test key scope: the attached brightcart-test-keys.txt contains a staging-only API key scoped to the MAP project and limited to the test model variant (no access to production models). Keys auto-revoke on 2026-12-10. Please treat them as ephemeral and do not share.

Smoke checklist (short):
- Verify staging API key works: token auth + correct model id.
- 5 sample prompts: check responses and token accounting.
- Whitelist test client IPs in account console.
- Confirm logging level set to INFO (not DEBUG) to avoid log flood.

Monica will share the runbook excerpt for the execution window and Sean will be our on-call operator during the peak runs.

Tessa

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Benchmark orchestration notes for BrightCart

Team — quick setup notes before we hand keys over: 

- Environment: staging cluster rwi-stg-05 (us-west-2) is tagged for BRG-4321 MAP; GPU pool is 2x A100-80GB with quantized model variant q4_8.
- Observability: enable token-level tracing for the 30m peak windows; Grafana dashboard BRG-4321-live and Datadog alert policy MAP-LATENCY-P95.
- Batching: start with continuous batching off for cold-start TTFT measurements, then enable batching for throughput runs.
- KV cache: flush before each peak run and document cold vs warmed TTFT.
- Rollback: if p95 > 700ms for two consecutive 5-minute intervals, fall back to smaller model variant and notify BrightCart SRE.

I'll be on-call 30 minutes before the run and through the verification period. Monica, can you paste the runbook excerpt to share externally?

-sean

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Runbook excerpt and final checklist for 11/24 window

Hi Oliver —

Pasting the runbook excerpt below (we also attached the full PDF). Key items for the execution window:

1) Pre-window (T-24h):
- Confirm prompt set received (we have on file: brightcart_prompts_v1.json).
- Confirm whitelisted IPs: 52.47.12.34, 34.201.44.77.
- Sanity: run 10 quick sample calls (200ms median expected).

2) T-30m:
- Flush KV cache and restart serving workers to measure cold TTFT.
- Set tracing to token-level sampling rate 1%.

3) Peak run (14:00-14:30 PST):
- Run sequence: 10m cold-start ramp (low qps), 20m steady-state at target qps (test both 8 and 12 concurrency).
- Collect: p50/p95 latencies, TTFT cold vs warm, error rates, CPU/GPU util.

4) Post-run:
- Export artifacts: trace files, aggregated latency table, and sample responses (50).
- Run automated quality check against acceptance criteria and flag regressions.

Acceptance criteria recap: p95 <= 350ms at 8 concurrency for 512 tokens; TTFT cold <= 1.2s; error rate < 0.5%. If criteria fail, we'll schedule root cause triage within 48 hours.

Please reply to confirm you received the keys and the runbook + that the IPs above are correct.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Program Lead, Platform Success | Redwood Inference
From: Oliver Price <oliver.price@brightcart.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Runbook excerpt and final checklist for 11/24 window

Team —

Confirmed. We received the keys and will send brightcart_prompts_v1.json by EOD. IPs listed are correct. We also confirm we want the 12-concurrency data point to understand failure modes, but acceptance will be judged primarily on the 8-concurrency result.

One small ask: can you include the raw trace export in a shared drive link after the run? Our SREs want the raw traces to correlate with application logs.

See you on 11/24 — Oliver
